html:
The Hunkpapa are one of the seven bands of the Lakota, the western branch of the Sioux. Their name means "head of the circle": when the Sioux met in great council, the Hunkpapa camped at its entrance.

In the 1700s and 1800s they hunted bison on horseback on the northern Great Plains, between the Missouri and the Yellowstone rivers. Their best known leader was Sitting Bull, with the war chief Gall. Hunkpapa warriors fought at the Little Bighorn in 1876. Sitting Bull then led his people into Canada for four years before surrendering in 1881. He was killed by Indian police at Standing Rock in 1890, two weeks before the Wounded Knee massacre.

Most Hunkpapa today live on the Standing Rock Reservation in the Dakotas. See also Lakota.
